state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me ask you this: what would happen if you tried your method on a simpler version of the problem?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I guess I could try it with just two plants, like \( 10 \mathrm{~cm} \) and \( 20 \mathrm{~cm} \). If I cut them in half, they'd be \( 5 \mathrm{~cm} \) and \( 10 \mathrm{~cm} \), so the range would still be \( 5 \mathrm{~cm} \). But if I added \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) to both, they'd be \( 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) and \( 23 \mathrm{~cm} \), and the range would still be \( 10 \mathrm{~cm} \). I’m not sure why that works differently for Katie's idea though. Can you help me understand that?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me ask you this: why do you think the range changed when you increased the heights by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) but stayed the same when you cut them in half?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher fails to address that the student's calculation in Turn 2 is actually correct (both operations preserve the range of 10), missing the real misconception, and the final question reinforces a false premise that the range changed when it didn't.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking without giving direct answers, perfectly exemplifying the Socratic method by having the student work through a simpler case and then questioning their interpretation of the results.
